title: 'Flames' video effect during Alan Peter's prayer stricken from Senate records
summary: The Senate impeachment court ordered Thursday the removal from its livestream video record the flames transition effect which appeared during a portion of the opening prayer led by Senator Alan Peter…

blocks.text: The Senate impeachment court ordered Thursday the removal from its livestream video record the flames transition effect which appeared during a portion of the opening prayer led by Senator Alan Peter Cayetano.
Presiding Officer Francis "Chiz" Escudero issued the order on Day 44 of the Senate impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, hours after the incident occured.

"I would like to instruct the Clerk of Court to kindly instruct the PRIB to be mindful or careful, with respect to the transition effects," Escudero said, referring to the Senate's Public Relations and Information Bureau.
Escudero added, "The flames are not well taken and inappropriate to these proceedings... Remove and edit it out from the records of the impeachment court."
Flames appeared onscreen as Cayetano prayed for the integrity of the Senate, acting as impeachment court, in the trial.

"As we humble ourselves to you today, we ask that we learn to look at ourselves first, our institutions, our intentions. Lord, again, we ask that you make the evidence so, so, so clear [...] Make it very clear whether a conviction is in order or an acquittal," he said, when the flames appeared on the screen.
The video feed appeared glitchy when the transition effects appeared.
Meanwhile, the Senate PRIB has issued an apology over the "accidental transition effect," saying it was due to an "unexpected technical issue."

The second week of the presentation of evidence of the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte is expected to feature four witnesses who will testify on the status of Cale88 Foods Corporation, a declared asset of the Vice President’s husband, Atty. Manases Carpio. — VDV, GMA News
